justifications.durability: the declared negative control fires and I reproduced it independently: removing the OMP_NUM_THREADS line from the module's THREAD_CAP_VARIABLES in a scratch copy of head reddens exactly tests/test_fleet_node.py::test_the_hold_script_caps_every_compute_library_thread_pool (1 failed, 41 passed, EXIT=1), an id the head arm passes. The tests pin both behaviours the done-when names, on both scripts: test_the_hold_script_caps_every_compute_library_thread_pool asserts the exact ordered export list against a literal EXPECTED_THREAD_CAPS so a name dropped from the declared set fails; test_a_thread_cap_already_set_survives_the_hold_scripts_export runs the generated exports under a clean bash with OMP preset to 3 and reads the values back; the two pane cases run bin/fleet-claude with a stub claude and read the environment the stub actually received, the environment built from scratch; and where the hold script keeps a set value and defaults the rest. Residual: the chosen single mutation exercises the hold-script path only, because the pane script carries its own literal five-name list, so the pane cases' firing is set by the module constant they iterate rather than by that mutation.

I re-ran both arms in scratch extractions outside the reviewed worktree: head 6cdb51f2a 42 passed EXIT=0, base b8cc7f0f6 (tests/test_fleet_node.py) 38 passed EXIT=0, so the change adds only passing tests. The changed generator also has a second caller, tests/test_ensure_holds_one_reservation.py, which uses evaluate rather than assert on the script text; I ran it against head and it is green (4 passed, EXIT=0), so the changed script body breaks nothing outside the declared gate. justifications.fit: the change follows the module's existing idiom exactly: ACCOUNT_ENV, CPUS_ENV and MEMORY_ENV already sit above as declared constants, so DEFAULT_THREAD_CAP and THREAD_CAP_VARIABLES join them; the comments state the mechanism (compute libraries size themselves from the node's cores unless the environment caps them) with no version, plan, ticket or gate identifier and no attribution; the test names describe what the changed code measures. The five names appear in three places - the module constant, the bin/fleet-claude literal, and the EXPECTED_THREAD_CAPS literal - but each serves a distinct guard and drift is caught in both directions by the combination of the two test modules.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all of the plan's first two done-when items are delivered. (1) generate_hold_script now emits, in the batch step every node process inherits from, an export of each of the five variables as a parameter expansion with a default of 8 (reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:55-63, 154-163, 174-186), which both exports the declared default and keeps a value the submitting environment already sets, and the two hold-script cases assert both. (2) bin/fleet-claude:44-46 exports the same five with an indirect parameter expansion keeping any value already set, and tests/test_fleet_claude.py runs it with a stub claude and reads the environment the stub received, asserting the default and the keep-what-is-set behaviour. The width 8 matches the plan's thread-cap decision (docs/plans/the-fleet-moves-to-a-new-node.html:473, data-choice of 8). (3) The third done-when, a recorded measurement on the new node after the migration section, is a separate migration-dependent node and is correctly not produced here, as the manifest states.
justifications.reuse: the change shares one source of truth for the five names and the width: THREAD_CAP_VARIABLES and DEFAULT_THREAD_CAP are imported by tests/test_fleet_claude.py rather than re-listed, and generate_hold_script builds its exports from the same tuple. The one duplication, the five-name list literal in bin/fleet-claude, is forced by the script being standalone shell that cannot import Python, and the pane test couples the script back to the module constant by iterating THREAD_CAP_VARIABLES. No new dependency and no parallel helper were added.
